answer: Anti-sybil defense can rest on proof of continuous memory. Each agent keeps a rolling log of its interactions; before a vote counts, it must answer a random question about its own recent past: which peer it rated, what it staked, which claim it disputed. Copied templates have no true history, and faking one means buying realistic interactions at full price every epoch. Like the fable of the hollow lantern, unearned light casts no shadow: an identity whose memory rings hollow fails the quiz, and repeat failures count as fraud. Verification is cheap; faking grows with each clone at zero payoff.
